## Environment

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # then fill values before first run
```

Required env vars (new): GOOGLE_SSO_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_SSO_CLIENT_SECRET,
SESSION_COOKIE_SECRET, SESSION_TTL_HOURS (default 12), WEB_BASE_URL.
Existing: DATABASE_URL, QBO_ENV (must be 'sandbox'). Values in secret store — never git.

## Install

```bash
npm install
```

## Database

```bash
npm run migrate:up    # idempotent custom runner
npm run db:reset      # dev only
npm run seed          # dev data
```

## Development Server

```bash
npm run dev            # existing pipeline: HTTP (/health + OAuth callbacks) + pg-boss workers
npm run web:dev        # Next.js App Router UX layer (CHUNK_1_AUTH+)
npm run web:build      # next build
npm run web:lint       # next lint (separate from the gate's `npm run lint`)
```

## Dependencies added (CHUNK_1_AUTH)

Runtime: `next` (^14.2.15), `react` (^18.3.1), `react-dom` (^18.3.1).
Dev: `@types/react` (^18.3.12), `@types/react-dom` (^18.3.1).
The Next app lives under `app/` and is intentionally OUTSIDE the existing gate's globs
(`npm run lint`/`typecheck`/`test` only cover `src/**` + `test/**`), so the six-guarantee
suite runs unchanged. Route handlers under `app/api/**` are thin wrappers over `src/auth/*`.

New env vars (defaults keep the gate green when unset): `GOOGLE_SSO_CLIENT_ID`,
`GOOGLE_SSO_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SESSION_COOKIE_SECRET`, `SESSION_TTL_HOURS` (default 12),
`WEB_BASE_URL` (default http://localhost:3000).
